title: Flag vs tackle: what changes
summary: Same game, smaller field, no tackling, and no blocking.

steps.text: Flag football is the same game with one big change: nobody tackles. Every player wears a belt with two flags. A ball carrier is down when a defender pulls one of the flags off.
The field is smaller. A 5v5 flag field is 50 yards long plus 10-yard end zones, and only 30 yards wide. In this game the flag field counts up from 10 to 40 so you always know how far you have gone.

Only 5 players per team are on the field, and in most youth leagues there is no blocking at all. That means everyone on offense is a receiver, even the center. He snaps the ball and then runs a route.
Since nobody blocks, only one defender is allowed to chase the quarterback: the rusher. He has to start 7 yards back from the line of scrimmage. Everyone else covers receivers.

A few more differences. The quarterback cannot run the ball past the line himself. There are no-run zones near the goal line, so teams must pass there. And a touchdown is still 6 points, so the goal is the same: get the ball in the end zone.

quiz.prompt: How is a ball carrier stopped in flag football?
quiz.explanation: Pull the flag off the belt and the play is over. No tackling.

quiz.prompt: How many players per team are on the field in 5v5 flag?
quiz.explanation: Five per side. Tackle football uses 11.

quiz.prompt: In youth flag football, what is the center allowed to do after the snap?
choices: Run a route and catch a pass
quiz.explanation: There is no blocking, so the center becomes a receiver after the snap.

quiz.prompt: Tap the only defender who is allowed to chase the quarterback.
quiz.explanation: That is the rusher. He starts 7 yards back and is the only one who can go after the quarterback.

quiz.prompt: How far back must the rusher start?
quiz.explanation: Seven yards from the line of scrimmage. That gives the quarterback a moment to throw.
